styleLock.name: locked-B watercolor
characteristics: soft atmospheric depth and tactile wear

padding.fill: median warm-paper color sampled from source corners

travelingCinemaVan: Use one compact, softly rounded, vintage-inspired utility body with a consistent wheelbase, wheel scale, door placement, lamps, mirrors, bumpers, hinges, seams, and roof vent.
The upper body is cream and the lower body is muted teal, divided by one continuous horizontal paint break.
The visible side carries a blank ivory screen deployed from a plain roof-edge housing with two mechanically plausible articulated braces.
Rear equipment access uses one large outward-opening door and fixed shelves sized for reels, cases, cables, and tools.
No badge, emblem, branded grille, license text, or plate-like readable mark is canonical.
projectorAndFilmKit: The projector is a compact hand-crank unit with a dark-walnut body and base, aged-brass lens, gate, sprockets, reel arms, ventilation, crank, and stable feet.
The crank remains on the same side and the two-reel film path remains mechanically legible across views.
Film tins are plain, dented, round metal containers distinguished only by removable cloth knots in muted rust, teal, ochre, or dusty blue.
The kit includes two empty spoked reels, a hinged metal splicer, blank perforated film leader, and a brown leather tool roll.
All plates, tins, handles, and tools remain unmarked.
oldCinema: All vignettes depict one modest neighborhood cinema with faded cream walls, restrained muted-teal lower-wall trim, dark worn wood, and rain-darkened service paving.
The projection booth uses square projection ports, a wood workbench, the canonical projector, plain film tins, cable hooks, and one amber task lamp.
The auditorium uses rows of worn muted-red seats, scuffed dark-wood armrests, a central aisle, and one blank taut ivory screen.
The shallow stage, curtain track, booth ports, service door, alley, folding ramp, and loading position must remain spatially compatible.
The alley van follows the traveling-cinema-van geometry and palette.
moodSheet: Use exactly ten unlabelled environment vignettes in two rows of five.
Separate vignettes only with warm-paper gutters; do not add boxes, captions, numbers, swatches, frames, or UI.
Read order is left-to-right across the top row, then left-to-right across the bottom row.
Each location remains original and anonymous, with no recognizable landmark or branded architecture.

rendering: Weathering is soft and use-based, not distressed branding.
Blank surfaces remain visually blank without pseudo-text texture.

originalityRestrictions: Do not reproduce or closely imitate an existing film, television, game, vehicle, projector, cinema, observatory, lighthouse, archive, or landmark design.
Do not introduce brands, logos, emblems, badges, trademarks, maker plates, license text, or branded color blocking.
Do not include readable text, pseudo-text, labels, handwriting, letters, numbers, posters, marquees, signs, or film-title imagery.
Do not include Cat, a mascot, people, animals, or character likenesses.
Do not include UI, icons, storyboard framing, film frames, decorative borders, panel borders, signatures, or watermarks.
The locked references authorize style cues only; their subjects, objects, layouts, compositions, architecture, typography, and borders are excluded.
Blank screens, storage spines, tins, plates, crates, terminals, and vehicle surfaces must remain blank.
These references are continuity guides, not legal clearance for later third-party additions.
